papers.title: Substance P-embedded multilayer on titanium substrates promotes local osseointegration via MSC recruitment.
papers.abstract: In this study, the chemokine substance P (SP) was inserted into multilayered systems on titanium (Ti)-based substrates for endogenous mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) recruitment to facilitate bone healing. The multilayer was constructed with cationic chitosan (Chi), SP and anionic gelatin (Gel) via a spin-coater-assisted layer-by-layer (LBL) approach. The characterization results demonstrated that the multilayer system was successfully constructed and was capable of continuously releasing SP for almost 2 weeks. We further confirmed that MSCs grown on SP-modified Ti-based substrates showed improved migration capabilities as well as enhanced secretion of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP2, MMP9), rather than enhanced MSC proliferation and differentiation in vitro. In the CD29+/CD90+ double immunofluorescence assay, the Ti/LBL-SP group showed the highest number of MSCs migrating to the peri-implant area after implantation. Consistently, the Ti/LBL-SP implants also significantly enhanced new bone formation according to the results of micro-CT scanning analysis, H&E staining, Masson's trichrome staining and immunohistochemical staining. The obtained results reveal that SP-modified Ti-based substrates were beneficial for bone formation via recruiting endogenous MSCs.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了钛基底上的物质P涂层以促进骨整合，但未涉及增材制造、多孔结构或力学性能测试。
llm.why_not_core: No AM/LPBF fabrication, no porous structure or stiffness matching design, no mechanical testing or fatigue evaluation, no stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 促进钛植入物骨整合，通过招募内源性干细胞。
summary_zh.method: 旋涂辅助逐层组装方法将物质P嵌入壳聚糖/明胶多层膜中。
summary_zh.result: 物质P涂层在体内外均增强干细胞迁移和新骨形成。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞迁移实验和体内大鼠植入模型。

summary_en.motivation: To improve osseointegration of titanium implants by recruiting endogenous mesenchymal stem cells via sustained release of substance P.
summary_en.method: Substance P was embedded in a chitosan/gelatin multilayer on titanium via spin-coater-assisted layer-by-layer assembly.
summary_en.result: The SP-modified coating enhanced MSC migration and new bone formation in a rat model without affecting proliferation.
summary_en.validation: In vitro migration assays and in vivo rat implantation with micro-CT, histological staining, and immunofluorescence.

papers.title: Biomechanical analysis of single-level interbody fusion with different internal fixation rod materials: a finite element analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lumbar spinal fusion with rigid spinal fixators as one of the high risk factors related to adjacent-segment failure. The purpose of this study is to investigate how the material properties of spinal fixation rods influence the biomechanical behavior at the instrumented and adjacent levels through the use of the finite element method. METHODS: Five finite element models were constructed in our study to simulate the human spine pre- and post-surgery. For the four post-surgical models, the spines were implanted with rods made of three different materials: (i) titanium rod, (ii) PEEK rod with interbody PEEK cage, (iii) Biodegradable rod with interbody PEEK cage, and (iv) PEEK cage without pedicle screw fixation (no rods). RESULTS: Fusion of the lumbar spine using PEEK or biodegradable rods allowed a similar ROM at both the fusion and adjacent levels under all conditions. The models with PEEK and biodegradable rods also showed a similar increase in contact forces at adjacent facet joints, but both were less than the model with a titanium rod. CONCLUSIONS: Flexible rods or cages with non-instrumented fusion can mitigate the increased contact forces on adjacent facet joints typically found following spinal fixation, and could also reduce the level of stress shielding at the bone graft.

llm.why_not_core: No hip implant or femoral stem analysis; no proximal femur stress shielding or micromotion quantification; no contact mechanics or patient-specific femur modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究不同脊柱固定棒材料对融合节段和邻近节段生物力学的影响
summary_zh.method: 构建五个腰椎有限元模型，比较钛棒、PEEK棒、生物降解棒和无棒融合的力学响应
summary_zh.result: 柔性棒或非固定融合可降低邻近小关节接触力，减少应力遮挡
summary_zh.validation: 有限元仿真验证，无实验数据

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how the material properties of spinal fixation rods influence biomechanical behavior at instrumented and adjacent levels in lumbar fusion.
summary_en.method: Five finite element models of the lumbar spine were constructed, comparing titanium rods, PEEK rods, biodegradable rods, and non-instrumented fusion.
summary_en.result: Flexible rods or cage-only fusion reduced adjacent facet joint contact forces and mitigated stress shielding at the bone graft.
summary_en.validation: Finite element simulation without experimental validation.
